sections.content: Scope decides where a name is visible. Variables declared inside a function usually exist only there — they are local. Variables outside are global, visible everywhere (use them sparingly).
Local scope prevents name collisions and makes functions predictable: two functions can each have a variable named total without interfering.
Key points: a function sees its own locals plus outer globals, but outer code cannot see inside the function.
